title: Never Stop Driving #196: Monterey Auctions
summary: Today marks the midpoint of a critical long weekend for the upper reaches of the classic car world. Five live auctions happening across California’s Monterey Peninsula will provide a vivid snapshot of the overall market. If you want to get in on the action, you don’t have to be in California, you can just stay […]
body_text: Today marks the midpoint of a critical long weekend for the upper reaches of the classic car world. Five live auctions happening across California’s Monterey Peninsula will provide a vivid snapshot of the overall market. If you want to get in on the action, you don’t have to be in California, you can just stay tuned to our blow-by-blow coverage of the Monterey auctions that will be continually updated as Hagerty experts weigh in on impactful sales and provide commentary. Live classic-car auctions, like the ones at Monterey, are fascinating events, and I learn something new every time I attend one. I’ve witnessed folks buying cars for tens of millions while the room remains church-quiet. I thought there’d be some high fives or at least a celebratory whoop, but that’s the exception. I’ve also learned about the politics of bidding. For example, highly knowledgeable collectors of a particular marque or genre of cars might not want others to know they’re bidding on a car. Why? Because the very fact they are bidding on the car can affirm the car’s quality, casting an aura of desirability and thus inciting competitors, which could drive up the price. This year, about a half-billion dollars’ worth of cars will change hands in just a few days. Incredible. As reported on the Hagerty live blog, the number of modern supercars sold during Monterey Car Week continues to grow, which is a major shift: 20 years ago, the big money flowed to cars produced before WWII. This year, modern supercars could make up 60% of sales. I should have bought a Ferrari Enzo when they were only a million dollars! hymanltd | Bring A Trailer A good example of how modern supercars are defining the market is a recent sale of a 2006 Ford GT Heritage Edition for $2.1 million . The GT’s sticker price in 2006 was around $175,000. Over the past two decades, this GT has been driven only eight miles and is essentially still new. It’s what’s known as a “wrapper” car, meaning it’s in the same condition as when it was inside as-delivered wrapping. Furthermore, it’s one of 343 Ford GTs with the fetching Gulf Oil livery. In short, the auction car is likely the most desirable example in existence and thus worth a premium over the $1.3 million value our team assigns to other concours-quality Ford GTs. Market watchers, however, were surprised by just how big that premium was. That’s because the Ford GT is not a rare car. Ford sold just over 4000 GTs between 2004 and 2006. Rarity is a prime driver in classic-car values, but absent rarity, desirability becomes the dominant factor. More people are falling for the mid-aughts Ford GT and, as we’ve noted, modern supercars in general. Let me do a victory lap here and remind you that we long ago predicted the Ford GT’s rise, having placed the car on the Hagerty Bull Market list , our annual prediction of cars that are rising in value, back in 2021. Yup, only five years ago, you could nab a very nice Ford GT for a few hundred grand, so it made sense to me that they’d eventually rise in value. James Lipman Sure, Ford produced thousands, but when I originally tested the car and met the engineers behind it, I realized how seriously they took their mission to re-create the sports car that brought Ford Le Mans victory in 1966. It’s gorgeous, well-engineered, and ridiculously fun to drive. Offered only with a manual transmission, it’s one of the few analog modern supercars, and car fans have noticed. Broad Arrow While the top of the market is rising, the rest is by and large not following. Hagerty’s market rating hasn’t moved much the whole year , which suggests a relatively stable market. That rating considers the entire market, which prompted us to wonder if there’s a K-shaped economy emerging for classic cars. Check out our live blog all weekend for real-time updates and be sure to read some of the latest from Hagerty: Vintage SUVs tackle the Baja 1000 course. Legal street racing on Detroit’s Woodward Avenue. A four-door Mustang sedan is coming. Porsche’s Jewish cofounder finally gets deserved credit. Never Stop Driving, Larry P.S.: Please share this newsletter with your car-obsessed friends and encourage them to sign up for the free weekly email. The easy-to-complete form is here . And if you’d like to support the efforts of Hagerty Media and receive the award-winning Hagerty Drivers Club magazine, please consider joining the Hagerty Drivers Club . title: Luvox for OCD: Uses, Dosage, and Side Effects
summary: Learn how Luvox (fluvoxamine) helps treat OCD, including how it works, recommended dosing, common side effects, safety warnings, and treatment guidance.
body_text: Key Takeaways Luvox (fluvoxamine) is among the few medications approved by the FDA for the treatment of obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) in both adults and children aged 8 years and older. Luvox helps regulate serotonin levels in the brain, which can reduce intrusive thoughts and compulsive behaviors associated with OCD. While Luvox can be effective for OCD, it may take 8 to 12 weeks to see significant improvement, and many people benefit most when medication is combined with therapy. Intrusive thoughts and repetitive behaviors make everyday life feel exhausting. If your healthcare provider recently prescribed Luvox for OCD, you may be wondering how it works, how long it takes to help, and what side effects to expect. Luvox is the brand name for fluvoxamine maleate, a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to treat obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) in adults and children aged 8 and older. While many people recognize SSRIs as medications used for depression, some are also highly effective for anxiety-related conditions, including OCD. If you're considering Luvox or have already started treatment, understanding how it works can help you feel more informed and confident about your next steps. How Luvox Works in the Brain Luvox, a SSRI, works by increasing the amount of serotonin available in the brain, which can help reduce the obsessive thoughts and compulsive behaviors in people diagnosed with OCD. Serotonin is a chemical messenger that helps regulate mood, emotions, and behavior. Normally, nerve cells release serotonin and then reabsorb it, but Luvox slows that reabsorption process, leaving more serotonin available to support communication between brain cells. Researchers don't fully understand the exact cause of OCD, but according to MedlinePlus , serotonin plays an important role in the condition, and by helping regulate serotonin activity, Luvox may reduce the intensity and frequency of obsessions and compulsions over time. One of the most important things to know is that improvement doesn't happen immediately. According to the National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH) , people taking antidepressants for OCD may need 8 to 12 weeks before they notice meaningful symptom improvement, and treatment often requires higher doses than those commonly used for depression. "Patients can notice mild to moderate improvement in mood and anxiety within the first 4-6 weeks of starting Luvox, but it may take up to 2-3 months to see the full benefit of a particular dose. While lower doses of Luvox can help OCD symptoms, some patients may need more time to get to the higher doses typically effective for OCD." - Anita Verma, M.D. Approved Medical Conditions for Luvox Treatment Luvox is FDA-approved to treat obsessive-compulsive disorder in adults and children aged 8 through 17. While Luvox can help reduce OCD symptoms, it doesn't eliminate stressors, resolve relationship concerns, or replace coping skills learned in therapy. "SSRIs like Luvox can be very helpful for decreasing the intensity of OCD symptoms. Combining this with specialized therapy approaches for OCD can help patients develop the tools they need to manage the OCD symptoms that affect their day-to-day lives." - Anita Verma, M.D. For many people, OCD medication works best as part of a comprehensive treatment plan. In addition to its approved use, fluvoxamine has been studied for several anxiety-related conditions, including social anxiety disorder. However, these uses are considered off-label in the U.S., meaning they aren't FDA-approved indications for fluvoxamine tablets. OCD in adults OCD can affect work, relationships, school performance, and overall quality of life. Adults with OCD often experience recurring fears, doubts, or unwanted thoughts that lead to repetitive actions such as checking, counting, cleaning, or seeking reassurance. When symptoms are persistent, distressing, or interfere with daily functioning, a healthcare provider may recommend medication such as Luvox alongside evidence-based therapy. The National Institute of Mental Health notes that exposure and response prevention (ERP), a specialized form of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), is an important component of long-term OCD management. OCD in children and adolescents Luvox is one of the few SSRIs approved for pediatric OCD, specifically in children and adolescents aged 8 to 17 when treatment is carefully monitored. Dosing in this group differs from adult protocols, and monitoring considerations are more intensive given the boxed warning for suicidal thinking in younger patients. Because OCD symptoms can affect development, school performance, family relationships, and social functioning, treatment often includes parents or caregivers. Therapy, school support, and regular follow-up visits can help children and teens build skills that support long-term symptom management. Standard Dosing Guidelines for Adults and Children Dosing for Luvox is individualized by a prescriber based on response, tolerability, and other medications. The information below is educational reference only and does not replace clinical guidance. Adult dosing recommendations For adults with OCD, FDA labeling for fluvoxamine tablets describes a starting dose of 50 mg taken at bedtime, with increases of 50 mg every 4 to 7 days as tolerated. For doses greater than 100 mg daily, providers may divide the medication into two doses taken at different times of day to improve tolerability. The maximum recommended daily dose for adults is 300 mg. For Luvox CR or extended-release, the FDA recommends a starting dose of 100 mg at bedtime, with weekly increases of 50 mg as tolerated to maximum effect, not to exceed 300 mg/day. Missed dose and administration timing If you miss a dose of Luvox, follow your healthcare provider's instructions or the medication guide provided with your prescription. In general, taking extra medication to make up for a missed dose is not recommended. How to Take Luvox Safely and Effectively Taking Luvox exactly as prescribed can help improve treatment results and reduce the risk of unwanted side effects. Try to take Luvox at the same time each day, as consistency helps maintain steady medication levels and may improve treatment effectiveness. If your provider recommends switching between once-daily and divided dosing schedules, make that change only under medical supervision. Luvox can generally be taken with or without food. If you experience nausea or stomach discomfort, taking it with food may help. If you're prescribed immediate-release tablets, swallow them whole with water unless your healthcare provider gives you different instructions. Extended-release capsules should also be swallowed whole and should not be crushed, chewed, or opened, as doing so can affect how the medication is released into your system. Do not stop taking Luvox suddenly. Like many SSRIs, fluvoxamine can cause discontinuation symptoms if stopped abruptly. These symptoms may include dizziness, irritability, nausea, headache, sleep disturbances, or flu-like symptoms. If you and your provider decide it's time to stop treatment, they'll typically recommend gradually reducing your dose over time. Common Side Effects You May Experience Most Luvox side effects are mild to moderate and often improve as your body adjusts to treatment. If side effects persist, worsen, or interfere with daily life, let your provider know. Sometimes adjusting the dose, changing the timing of medication, or making other treatment modifications can help. Digestive and gastrointestinal effects Digestive symptoms are among the most commonly reported side effects of Luvox. You may experience: Nausea Upset stomach Loss of appetite Diarrhea Constipation These symptoms often improve after the first few weeks of treatment. Taking Luvox with food may help reduce nausea for some people. Sleep and energy changes Luvox can affect sleep differently depending on the person. Some people experience: Drowsiness Fatigue Increased sleepiness Others may notice: Insomnia Restlessness Difficulty falling asleep Because responses vary, your provider may recommend adjusting when you take your medication if sleep-related side effects become troublesome. Sexual function considerations Changes in sexual function are a known side effect of many SSRIs, including Luvox. Potential effects may include: Reduced sexual desire Difficulty reaching orgasm Delayed ejaculation Erectile difficulties These side effects can feel frustrating or embarrassing, but they're common and important to discuss openly with your provider. In many cases, treatment adjustments can help. Don't stop taking medication without medical guidance because of sexual side effects alone. Serious Safety Warnings and When to Seek Help Although serious complications are uncommon, some Luvox side effects require immediate medical attention. Black-box warning for suicidal thoughts Like all antidepressants, Luvox carries an FDA boxed warning regarding an increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in children, adolescents, and young adults during the early stages of treatment or after dose changes. This warning doesn't mean everyone taking Luvox will experience these thoughts. However, you, your family members, and caregivers should remain alert for sudden changes in mood, behavior, or emotional well-being, including: Worsening depression Increased anxiety or agitation Panic symptoms Irritability Impulsive behavior Thoughts of self-harm Contact your healthcare provider immediately if any of these symptoms increase or develop suddenly. Serotonin syndrome risk Serotonin syndrome is a rare but potentially life-threatening condition caused by excessive serotonin activity in the nervous system. The risk increases when Luvox is combined with other medications that affect serotonin levels, including certain antidepressants, migraine medications, pain medications, and supplements. Symptoms may include: Confusion Agitation Rapid heart rate High fever Excessive sweating Muscle rigidity or twitching Tremors Loss of coordination Seek emergency medical care immediately if these symptoms occur. Mania and bipolar disorder considerations In some people with bipolar disorder, antidepressants may trigger episodes of mania or hypomania. Symptoms can include: Unusually elevated mood Increased energy Decreased need for sleep Racing thoughts Risky or impulsive behavior Before starting Luvox, your provider may assess whether you have a personal or family history of bipolar disorder. Severe allergic reactions Although rare, serious allergic reactions can occur. Seek emergency care if you develop: Difficulty breathing Swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat Severe rash Hives Who Should Not Take Luvox? Certain medical conditions and medication combinations may make Luvox unsafe or require additional monitoring. You should not take Luvox if you: Are currently taking a monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI) intended to treat psychiatric disorders Have taken an MAOI within the previous 14 days Plan to start an MAOI within 14 days of stopping Luvox Are being treated with linezolid or intravenous methylene blue Take tizanidine, thioridazine, pimozide, alosetron, or ramelteon Have had a previous allergic reaction to fluvoxamine Additional caution may be needed if you have: A seizure disorder Liver disease Bipolar disorder Bleeding disorders A history of low sodium levels Glaucoma Pregnancy or plans to become pregnant Luvox can also interact with many prescription medications because it affects several liver enzymes involved in drug metabolism. That's why it's important to provide your healthcare provider with a complete list of medications, supplements, and over-the-counter products before starting treatment. Monitoring Requirements During Treatment Regular follow-up appointments help ensure Luvox is working safely and effectively. Monitoring is especially important during the first few months of treatment and after any dose changes. Your provider will monitor: OCD symptom improvement Side effects Mood changes Thoughts of suicide Sleep patterns Medication interactions Children, teens, and young adults often require closer observation because of the FDA boxed warning. Caregivers should communicate any concerning behavioral or emotional changes promptly. Older adults may require additional monitoring because they're more vulnerable to certain side effects, including low sodium levels and medication interactions. Routine laboratory testing isn't required for everyone taking Luvox. However, testing may be recommended when underlying medical conditions, medication interactions, or specific side effects warrant additional evaluation. If you're participating in therapy alongside medication treatment, keeping both your therapist and psychiatric provider informed about symptom changes can help support coordinated care. Comparing Luvox to Other SSRI Medications Most SSRIs share a similar mechanism, but they differ in dosing flexibility, side effect profiles, FDA-approved uses, and drug interaction risks. One notable distinction is that fluvoxamine affects several liver enzymes involved in medication metabolism. As a result, it has more clinically significant drug interactions than some other SSRIs, making a thorough medication review especially important before treatment begins. Medication FDA-approved for OCD Notable consideration Luvox (fluvoxamine) Yes More medication interactions than many SSRIs Prozac (fluoxetine) Yes A longer half-life may reduce withdrawal symptoms Zoloft (sertraline) Yes Commonly prescribed for OCD and anxiety disorders Paxil (paroxetine) Yes Higher risk of discontinuation symptoms Lexapro (escitalopram) No Often prescribed for anxiety and depression Celexa (citalopram) No May require additional cardiac monitoring at higher doses No single SSRI is universally better than another. Some people respond well to the first medication they try, while others may need adjustments before finding the treatment that works best. Your provider will consider your medical history, symptom severity, other medications, and personal preferences when recommending treatment. If you're exploring medication options, learning more about SSRI antidepressant medications and OCD treatment approaches can help you have a more informed conversation with your provider. Manage OCD Symptoms With Online Psychiatry Support at Talkspace Luvox can be an effective treatment option for OCD, but finding the right medication and dosage often takes time and ongoing monitoring. Regular follow-up with a psychiatric provider helps ensure your treatment is effective, minimizes side effects, and addresses any concerns that may arise Talkspace connects members with licensed psychiatric providers who can evaluate OCD symptoms, prescribe medication when appropriate, and provide ongoing prescription management through a secure online platform. If you're exploring Luvox for OCD or considering other medication options, Talkspace can help you access personalized care from wherever you're most comfortable. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) What is Luvox, and how does it treat OCD? Luvox is the brand name for fluvoxamine, an FDA-approved SSRI used to treat obsessive-compulsive disorder in adults and children aged 8 and older. It works by increasing serotonin availability in the brain, which may help reduce obsessive thoughts and compulsive behaviors over time. How long does Luvox take to work for OCD? Luvox (fluvoxamine) typically takes about 2 to 4 weeks to start showing initial improvement in OCD symptoms. Full therapeutic effects often take 8 to 12 weeks or longer, as dosage is gradually adjusted and the brain adapts to the medication. What are the most common Luvox side effects? Common Luvox side effects include nausea, upset stomach, appetite changes, drowsiness, insomnia, and sexual side effects. Many of these symptoms improve during the first few weeks of treatment as your body adjusts to the medication. Can children and teens take Luvox for OCD? Yes, Luvox is FDA-approved for treating OCD in children and teens aged 8 and older. It should be prescribed and monitored by a healthcare provider to ensure effectiveness and manage potential side effects. Is Luvox safe to stop suddenly? No. Stopping Luvox abruptly can lead to discontinuation symptoms such as dizziness, nausea, irritability, headaches, and sleep disturbances. If you need to stop treatment, your healthcare provider will typically recommend gradually tapering the medication. Sources FDA. Fluvoxamine maleate tablets [prescribing information]. title: How to Use GPT, Gemini, and Grok Models Inside Claude Code with CLI Proxy
summary: Claude Code expects Claude models. CLI Proxy is a local proxy server that translates API formats both ways, so you can point Claude Code at GPT, Gemini, or Grok and keep skills, subagents, and reasoning efforts working.
body_text: TL;DR: CLI Proxy is a local proxy server that lets you run GPT, Gemini, or Grok models inside Claude Code by pointing ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN at localhost:8317 It logs in through each provider's OAuth flow, so requests draw from your existing subscription instead of pay-as-you-go API credits Each Claude Code tier ( ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL , SONNET , HAIKU ) can map to a different model from a different provider Skills, subagents, reasoning efforts, and plan mode all keep working because translation happens at the API layer The proxy stores multiple OAuth tokens per provider and rotates between them (default: round-robin) to spread usage across accounts Exposing Claude models to other CLIs technically violates Anthropic's ToS; using non-Claude models inside Claude Code (the direction covered here) doesn't Claude Code is my pick for the best AI coding tool right now, and it expects you to use Claude models, which cost more than the competition and come with less generous subscription limits. There's a way around that: CLI Proxy , a local proxy server that lets you run GPT , Gemini , or Grok models inside Claude Code, on your existing subscriptions. It also switches between multiple accounts for the same provider automatically, so you get more out of your usage limits. Here's how the whole thing works. Claude Code running a GPT model This is Claude Code, except the model in the status line is gpt-5.6-terra instead of a Claude model. Ask it don't use any skills, what ai model is this and who was it built by and it answers GPT-5.6 Terra, built by OpenAI . You can swap between models, Terra, Luna, and Sol here, and change the reasoning effort level, without leaving Claude Code. The API Usage Billing notice is a red herring: the requests come out of your provider subscription rather than pay-as-you-go API credits, for reasons that make sense once you see how the authentication works . Everything else about Claude Code behaves normally. Giving it a real task, search for information about Opus 5 and present it to me in an Anthropic style HTML page , it loads a skill , thinks with medium effort, and runs the task with full subagent support. Part of that task was gathering current information about a model that didn't exist when the GPT model was trained, which it did through the new and improved Firecrawl search API . Search is one of the endpoints that works keyless , so there's nothing to sign up for to try it, though a free API key raises the rate limits and adds credits. Search is what this run needed; /scrape returns clean markdown from a single URL, and /interact handles pages that need clicks or logins before you can extract. The result was a full status page, built by an OpenAI model, researched with Firecrawl , orchestrated entirely by Claude Code. You can see the page it generated , complete with a lineup map, an evidence ledger, and a timeline. It's demo output rather than a reference, so none of it has been fact-checked. That whole run cost 11% of the weekly subscription limit. Claude Code reported a much higher context figure than that, which is a small display bug in the setup rather than real usage. Installing CLI Proxy On a Mac, CLI Proxy installs through Homebrew: brew install cliproxyapi brew services start cliproxyapi Linux has a one-click installer script and an AUR package, Windows has a release binary plus a desktop GUI, and there's a Docker image if you'd rather run this on a separate VPS. All four paths are in the quick start docs . Editing the CLI Proxy config Where the config file lives depends on how you installed it. With Homebrew on Apple Silicon it's at /opt/homebrew/etc/cliproxyapi.conf . Two things in there need changing. # /opt/homebrew/etc/cliproxyapi.conf port : 8317 remote-management : # Password for the web UI. Put a plaintext value here and it gets # hashed on startup. secret-key : "something-you-will-remember" # Authentication directory (supports ~ for home directory) auth-dir : "~/.cli-proxy-api" # API keys for authentication api-keys : - "sk-your-api-key-1" The secret-key is the password you'll use to log into CLI Proxy's web view. It can be anything, and it gets hashed inside the config the first time you log in, so it won't sit there in plaintext. The api-keys list is the more interesting one. This is the token that gets bundled with every request Claude Code sends to the proxy. Claude Code expects a token to exist, so you give it one of these, and CLI Proxy checks the incoming token against this list before doing anything real. It's what stops any other app on your machine from hitting the proxy port and burning through your usage. You can generate a proper random value for it rather than making one up: openssl rand -hex 32 Once the config is saved, restart the service to pick it up: brew services restart cliproxyapi Logging in a provider Now go to http://localhost:8317 and log in with the password you set as your secret key. That opens the CLI Proxy API Management Center , and from the dashboard, OAuth Login lists every provider you can authenticate with: Codex, Anthropic, Antigravity, and Kimi. Starting a Codex login opens the normal OAuth flow: pick your account, approve it, done. The page itself doesn't change afterwards, so to confirm it worked, head to Auth Files , where the credential shows up with its provider, size, and health. This is also where the multi-account part starts to matter. Nothing stops you logging in several times with different accounts for the same provider, and each one lands here as its own credential. Pointing Claude Code at the proxy The last step is configuring your client. Claude Code reads its endpoint and model choices from environment variables, so a shell alias is enough: # config.fish alias ccx = 'ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8317 \ ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=sk-your-api-key-1 \ ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL=gpt-5.6-terra \ ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL=gpt-5.6-terra \ ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL=gpt-5.6-luna \ ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL=gpt-5.6-sol \ CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=gpt-5.6-terra \ claude' Here's what each variable does: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points Claude Code at the local proxy instead of Anthropic's servers. ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN is one of the values from the api-keys list you set earlier. ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL , ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL , ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL , and ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL each map one Claude Code model tier onto the model you actually want running there. CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL covers what subagents get. They're all separate variables, so nothing stops you pointing each tier at a different provider. You can see the result in Claude Code's own model picker, which still thinks it's offering you Claude tiers and lists a GPT model against each one: If you're not sure what model names to put in those variables, ask the proxy. It exposes an OpenAI-compatible models endpoint, and piping it through jq makes it readable: curl -s http://localhost:8317/v1/models \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-your-api-key-1" | jq Reload your shell config, run the alias, and Claude Code starts up on a GPT model. Claude Code isn't the only option either: CLI Proxy has client configuration docs for Codex , Factory Droid , and OpenCode too. If you have several clients pointed at the proxy, give each one a different API key from the list. That way the proxy's logs and quota tracking can tell them apart. One thing worth flagging: this works in the other direction as well. You could sign in with Anthropic OAuth and use your Claude subscription inside Codex. That technically goes against Claude's terms of service though, so it's not something to recommend. How CLI Proxy translates between APIs At a high level, CLI Proxy is a proxy server that lets a client like Claude Code read the API format of a different model. Normally, a prompt in Claude Code goes to Anthropic's servers and comes back in Anthropic's API format, which Claude Code knows how to read. Send a prompt from Codex CLI and it goes to OpenAI's servers and comes back in OpenAI's format, which Claude Code can't read. Same request, incompatible envelope. CLI Proxy sits between the client and the model provider's servers and translates in both directions: your request becomes something the provider understands, and the provider's response becomes something the client understands. Because the translation happens at the API layer, everything built on top of the API survives the trip. That's why reasoning efforts , subagents , and Claude Code workflows all still work when the model on the other end is GPT. How CLI Proxy handles authentication The more interesting half of this is how CLI Proxy handles auth. When you log into a model provider's website to use your subscription, you get back a token that only that provider accepts. Tokens aren't interchangeable, which is normally the end of the conversation. When you log in through CLI Proxy, it grabs that token and saves it in its own auth directory. So a request from Claude Code carries the dummy token from CLI Proxy's config, because Claude Code insists on a token existing. CLI Proxy checks that token against its list, and if it matches, makes the real request using the real provider token it's holding. This is why the multi-account thing works. Since the proxy owns the real credentials, it can hold several accounts for the same provider and pick whichever token it likes per request. The default strategy is round-robin , which spreads load across accounts to get the most out of your rate limits. There's also fill-first if you'd rather exhaust one account before moving to the next, plus optional session affinity to bind a conversation to one credential. Why not just use GLM or Kimi directly This isn't an entirely new technique. Kimi and GLM already let you use their models inside Claude Code, and cc-mirror lets you create isolated versions of Claude Code with custom providers. The catch with those is that you're locked into one provider. You can't make your Fable model GPT, your Opus model GLM, and your Sonnet model Kimi. You use that provider's models for everything, or you use something else. And if you wanted to run this through Codex instead of Claude Code, some of those integrations won't work at all, because they don't support the API Codex speaks. Which is why Theo and even Tibo from OpenAI recommend CLI Proxy for running GPT models inside Claude Code. One local proxy, one config file, and the model behind each Claude Code tier becomes something you choose rather than something you inherit.

title: Research Frontiers Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Will Host a Conference Call at 4:30 p.m. Today
summary: WOODBURY, N.Y., August 6, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Research Frontiers Inc. (Nasdaq: REFR) announced its financial results for its second quarter of 2026. Management will host a conference call today...

Management will host a conference call today at 4:30 p.m. Eastern Time to discuss its financial and operating results as well as recent developments. Who: Joseph M. title: Jacobs named ENR's No. 1 airport design firm for second consecutive year
summary: For the second consecutive year, Jacobs has been ranked ENR's No. 1 design firm in the Airports category. The recognition reflects the company's work beyond major capital programs, spanning planning, airfield engineering, sustainability, digital transformation and operational readiness.
body_text: For the second consecutive year, Jacobs has been recognized by Engineering News-Record (ENR) as the No. 1 design firm in the Airports category, underscoring the company's leadership on complex airport infrastructure programs worldwide. This recognition reflects the scale and breadth of Jacobs’ airport design portfolio, which supports clients from strategy, airport planning and preconstruction through delivery, operational readiness and project closeout, as well as working with operators to maintain safe and efficient airport operations throughout construction. Airports around the world continue to navigate significant periods of change. Rising passenger demand, aging infrastructure, climate pressures and rapidly evolving technology are reshaping how airports are planned, built and operated. Beyond major capital programs, airport owners and operators increasingly need organizations that can bring together strategic advisory, planning, engineering, digital innovation, sustainability and operational readiness to improve performance throughout the life of an airport. This integrated approach is evident across Jacobs' aviation portfolio. Delivering transformation at scale As airports modernize and expand, delivering major capital programs while maintaining operations has become increasingly complex. Jacobs works with clients to increase capacity and improve passenger experience, building resilience through integrated planning, engineering and delivery services. Recent examples include Cleveland Hopkins International Airport's $1.6 billion CLEvolution modernization program , Hollywood Burbank Airport’s Replacement Passenger Terminal and London Gatwick Airport's capital investment program. These projects demonstrate how Jacobs supports airport owners to transform aging infrastructure while maintaining operational continuity. Supporting performance across the airport lifecycle Airport performance depends on more than terminals and vertical infrastructure. Airfields, runways, taxiways and operational systems play a critical role in maintaining safety, efficiency and reliability. Recent work includes major airfield investments at Denver International Airport and the modernization of the automated aerotrain system at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) in Malaysia. As project management consultant for the aerotrain replacement program, Jacobs supported planning, design, testing and commissioning of the airport's new driverless people mover system, improving passenger connectivity and operational reliability in addition to the overall airport experience. In India, Jacobs is supporting Noida International Airport as it prepares for future demand, integrating sustainability with planning and delivery from the earliest stages of development. Globally, our work combines near-term operational improvements with the resilience and capacity needed to support airports over the long term. Advancing airport sustainability and digital innovation Airports are increasingly leveraging sustainable practices and digital technologies to improve performance, reduce emissions and support long-term growth. Jacobs is supporting clients to integrate these capabilities from planning through operations. In the United Kingdom, Jacobs is applying digital insight to Heathrow Airport's decarbonization program. Heathrow's Marginal Abatement Cost Curve (MACC) tool enables stakeholders to evaluate carbon reduction initiatives and prioritize investments based on emissions and cost impacts, providing greater confidence in long- term investment decisions. Similarly, at King Salman International Airport (KSIA) in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, Jacobs is working with the client to shape the future of operations through planning, runway design, sustainability integration and digital systems while defining a roadmap for smart operations, passenger experience, digital twin integration and cybersecurity. By bringing these capabilities together through a single integrated approach, we’re laying the foundation for a smarter, more connected and operationally efficient airport. Through integration of sustainability, digital innovation and operational insight, we’re supporting airport owners to build more resilient and future-ready aviation infrastructure. Preparing airports for operational success from day one Successful airport programs do not end when construction is complete. New facilities, systems and infrastructure must be ready to perform from the first day of operations. Through its Operational Readiness, Activation and Transition practice, Jacobs enables airports to align people, processes, systems and stakeholders to support a seamless transition from delivery to live operations. Recent activations at Pittsburgh International Airport and Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) demonstrate Jacobs’ ability to manage complex operational transitions while minimizing disruption and preparing staff, systems and facilities for day-one success. complex operational transitions while minimizing disruption and preparing staff, systems and facilities for day-one success. Together, these projects demonstrate why Jacobs continues to be recognized as a global aviation leader.

title: Amazon EC2 R8i and R8i-Flex instances are now available in Europe (Milan) region
summary: Discover more about what's new at AWS with Amazon EC2 R8i and R8i-Flex instances are now available in Europe (Milan) region
body_text: Starting today, Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) R8i and R8i-flex instances are available in the Europe (Milan) region. These instances are powered by custom Intel Xeon 6 processors, available only on AWS, delivering the highest performance and fastest memory bandwidth among comparable Intel processors in the cloud. The R8i and R8i-flex instances offer up to 15% better price-performance, and 2.5x more memory bandwidth compared to previous generation Intel-based instances. They deliver 20% higher performance than R7i instances, with even higher gains for specific workloads. They are up to 30% faster for PostgreSQL databases, up to 60% faster for NGINX web applications, and up to 40% faster for AI deep learning recommendation models compared to R7i. R8i-flex, our first memory-optimized Flex instances, are the easiest way to get price performance benefits for a majority of memory-intensive workloads. They offer the most common sizes, from large to 16xlarge, and are a great first choice for applications that don't fully utilize all compute resources. R8i instances are a great choice for all memory-intensive workloads, especially for workloads that need the largest instance sizes or continuous high CPU usage. R8i instances offer 13 sizes including 2 bare metal sizes and the new 96xlarge size for the largest applications. R8i instances are SAP-certified and deliver 142,100 aSAPS, the highest among all comparable machines in on-premises and cloud environments, delivering exceptional performance for mission-critical SAP workloads. To get started, sign in to the AWS Management Console . Customers can purchase these instances via Savings Plans, On-Demand instances, and Spot instances. For more information about the new R8i and R8i-flex instances visit the AWS News blog .

title: Lifetime Brands, Inc. Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results
summary: Declares Regular Quarterly Dividend GARDEN CITY, N.Y., Aug. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Lifetime Brands, Inc. (NasdaqGS: LCUT), a leading global...
body_text: Declares Regular Quarterly Dividend GARDEN CITY, N.Y., Aug. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Lifetime Brands, Inc. (NasdaqGS: LCUT), a leading global designer, developer and marketer of a broad range of branded consumer products used in the home, today reported its financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. Rob Kay, Lifetime's Chief Executive Officer, commented, “Our second quarter results were in line with expectations and reflected notable growth compared to the prior year period that had been adversely impacted by the U.S. government implementation of initial high tariff rates across many countries. Net sales were up 7.4% and we saw significant earnings growth that includes the expected recovery of tariffs we paid in 2025. We will put that capital to work, paying the associated taxes, restoring reductions that had been implemented in 2025 to increase our bottom line against the impact from these tariff expenses and to fund the investments to bolster competitiveness and restore the balance sheet strength which we have used to fund the carrying cost of tariffs paid. Accordingly, since the end of the first quarter, we have repaid $40 million of term debt using cash generated from operations and the receipt of tariff refunds. The underlying business performed well despite softer end markets, led by growth in warehouse club programs and e-commerce. The relaunch of our redesigned Farberware line is off to an encouraging start and we extended our Dolly Parton license for an additional three years, reflecting the continued strength of that partnership. Our International segment again narrowed its losses and remains on track to achieve break-even in 2026, and the Hagerstown facility is online. While this new facility is experiencing startup challenges, we remain targeted for full operation by the fourth quarter this year. For 2026, we are reaffirming our net sales guidance, and raising earnings guidance to reflect the recognition of the tariff refunds. As previously announced, we look forward to presenting our longer-term strategy at our upcoming Investor Day this December. Second Quarter Financial Results: Consolidated net sales for the three months ended June 30, 2026 were $141.6 million, representing an increase of $9.7 million, or 7.4%, as compared to net sales of $131.9 million for the corresponding period in 2025. In constant currency, a non-GAAP financial measure, which excludes the impact of foreign exchange fluctuations and was determined by applying 2026 average rates to 2025 local currency amounts, consolidated net sales increased by $9.5 million, or 7.2%, as compared to consolidated net sales in the corresponding period in 2025. A table reconciling this non-GAAP financial measure to consolidated net sales, as reported, is included below. Gross margin for the three months ended June 30, 2026 was $93.2 million, or 65.9%, as compared to $50.8 million, or 38.6%, for the corresponding period in 2025. Gross margin for the current period includes a tariff refund benefit of $40.1 million. Selling, general and administrative expenses for the three months ended June 30, 2026 were $39.5 million, an increase of $2.0 million, or 5.3%, as compared to $37.5 million for the corresponding period in 2025. Income from operations was $31.6 million, as compared to loss from operations of $(37.2) million for the corresponding period in 2025. Income from operations for the current period includes a tariff refund benefit of $40.1 million. Loss from operations for the prior period included a non-cash goodwill impairment charge of $33.2 million related to the U.S. segment. The 2026 period included adjustments for acquisition-related intangible amortization expense of $4.3 million, acquisition-related diligence expenses of $1.0 million, restructuring expenses of $2.0 million, and warehouse relocation and redesign expenses of $2.2 million. The 2025 period included adjustments for acquisition-related intangible amortization expense of $4.4 million, acquisition-related diligence expenses of $0.1 million, warehouse relocation and redesign expenses of $0.1 million, severance expenses of $0.3 million and goodwill impairment charge of $33.2 million. Net income was $19.6 million, or $0.87 per diluted share, as compared to net loss of $(39.7) million, or $(1.83) per diluted share, in the corresponding period in 2025. Net income for the current period included a pre-tax tariff refund benefit of $40.1 million. Net loss for the prior period included a non-cash goodwill impairment charge of $33.2 million. Adjusted net income(1) was $26.6 million, or $1.18 per diluted share, as compared to adjusted net loss of $(2.6) million, or $(0.12) per diluted share, in the corresponding period in 2025. Six Months Financial Results: Consolidated net sales for the six months ended June 30, 2026 were $285.1 million, an increase of $13.2 million, or 4.9%, as compared to net sales of $271.9 million for the corresponding period in 2025. In constant currency, a non-GAAP financial measure, which excludes the impact of foreign exchange fluctuations and was determined by applying 2026 average rates to 2025 local currency amounts, consolidated net sales increased by $12.0 million, or 4.4%, as compared to consolidated net sales in the corresponding period in 2025.
